what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Research should be delivered as a living vault
sections.para: Research sold by subscription arrives as frozen documents, one reading for every reader. Delivered as an sgit vault, it can carry findings with evidence, a graph, per-reader briefings, calculations, a custom app and a lane back. AI-enabled products need behaviour policies with and without the AI, and a synthetic example vault shows it working.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Vaults beat frozen reports; AI products need behaviour policies
sections.para: Instead of documents, deliver findings, evidence, a graph, briefings, calculations, an app and a lane back in a vault. A fractal graph goes beyond one taxonomy, and a behaviour policy with and without the AI shows what insurability turns on. Evidence can come from a governed agent hive, sold by the block.

sections.label: How research is sold today
sections.line: Research is sold by subscription and delivered as documents
sections.para: Gartner reported $6.5 billion of revenue for 2025, mostly from subscriptions of at least twelve months with 77% of contracts multi-year, and Forrester $396.9 million. Many smaller firms research single markets. Delivery is reports, portals and spreadsheets, and the newest layer, a chat over documents like Forrester's AI Access, is still the same product.

sections.label: One taxonomy is version one
sections.line: A taxonomy is version one; graphs carry the why
sections.para: Research catalogues rest on taxonomies like G2's categories, which say which vendors fit a category but not why a rating changed, what evidence supports it or what differs for one buyer. A fractal semantic graph links question, vendor, capabilities, rules, findings, evidence and the agent that produced it, and firms already hold most of that data.

sections.label: Deliver the research as a vault
sections.line: A vault delivers evidence, briefings, calculations, app and feedback
sections.para: A vault carries findings with their evidence, a queryable graph, briefings for the CISO, CFO, counsel, procurement, board and underwriter, editable calculations, a branded app and an append lane for client comments. Each vault has its own key, so access per client is nearly free, and a re-assessment arrives as a commit with a diff.

sections.label: AI-enabled products need a behaviour policy
sections.line: Adding AI changes reach, so write two policies
sections.para: Putting a model in front of an API is what OWASP calls Excessive Agency, shown by the Microsoft 365 Copilot zero-click leak and Salesforce's Agentforce data theft. Writing behaviour policies with and without the AI shows the difference: in the example, reach grows from four systems to six and three of eight rules rest only on the model.

sections.label: Licence to operate, and insurability
sections.line: Ratings over policy facts can show licence and insurability
sections.para: The policy describes and the research firm judges whether a product is licensed to operate and how insurable its risk is. Insurers already lean on security ratings, Lloyd's underwriters launched affirmative AI cover in 2025, and in November 2025 large insurers asked US regulators to exclude AI liabilities, so evidence of what AI changes matters.

sections.label: Evaluations with provenance
sections.line: Agent hives produce evaluations with provenance in a ledger
sections.para: ruv.sgit runs a Ruflo hive of Claude Code workers with a vault per run, a behaviour policy per role and a ledger of every action, and its client receives the run's vault. In the example, six workers ran 79 tasks and QA rejected two unsupported claims, the provenance an underwriter can rely on.

sections.label: The business model
sections.line: Sell research by the block, built on open source
sections.para: Research can be sold in blocks: a live evaluation, the vault for one product, a briefing per extra reader, a portfolio subscription refreshed as vendors ship, and a branded app. Client feedback from the lanes becomes the firm's best brief, and because the tooling is open source a firm can run it itself.

sections.label: The example vault
sections.line: A synthetic research vault shows the idea working
sections.para: The example has made-up Corvane Research assessing made-up Tallyfern Pay before and after its Copilot agent for a made-up buyer. Its thirteen pages cover two behaviour policies, the evaluation run and ledger, six findings, the fractal graph, the rating, six briefings, a cost calculator, the client's lane and the business model.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: The example is synthetic and the model untested
sections.para: The firm, product, buyer, findings and prices are invented, and the evaluation run follows ruv.sgit's ledger format without being real. ruv.sgit is not yet automated end to end, the grade is a judgement over shown facts, and no research firm is known to use this approach today.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: market results, AI risk and insurance reports
sections.para: The article came from two voice memos of 16 October 2026. It draws on Gartner's and Forrester's 2025 results, Forrester's AI Access, G2's research agenda, OWASP's Excessive Agency entry, CVE-2025-32711, The Register on ForcedLeak, insurance reporting including Armilla and Chaucer, and abp.sgit.ai and ruv.sgit.ai.
